_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for South Sudan covering Nilotic peoples, Shilluk Kingdom, Mahdist and Anglo-Egyptian Sudan, civil wars, CPA 2005, independence 2011 (world's newest country), civil war 2013-2020, and humanitarian crisis.

ethnic_groups.name: Dinka (Jieng)
ethnic_groups.notes: Largest group; Nilotic pastoralists; Bahr el Ghazal and Upper Nile; tall stature; cattle culture; Salva Kiir's group; multiple sections (Bor, Agar, Rek, Malual, Ngok)

ethnic_groups.name: Nuer (Naath)
ethnic_groups.notes: Nilotic pastoralists; Upper Nile and Jonglei; Evans-Pritchard anthropological studies; Riek Machar's group; cattle-centred culture; White Nile/Sobat

ethnic_groups.name: Shilluk (Chollo)
ethnic_groups.notes: Upper Nile; oldest kingdom in South Sudan (Reth/king tradition); Fashoda; Nilotic

ethnic_groups.name: Azande (Zande)
ethnic_groups.notes: Western Equatoria; non-Nilotic (Niger-Congo); historically formed kingdoms; witchcraft studies by Evans-Pritchard

ethnic_groups.name: Bari
ethnic_groups.notes: Central Equatoria; Juba area; farming; related groups: Mundari, Kuku, Kakwa, Pojulu

ethnic_groups.name: Murle
ethnic_groups.notes: Jonglei; historically cattle raiders; Pibor; conflict with Lou Nuer

ethnic_groups.name: Toposa
ethnic_groups.notes: Eastern Equatoria; Karamojong cluster; pastoralists; cross-border with Kenya/Uganda

ethnic_groups.name: Anuak
ethnic_groups.notes: Upper Nile; Nilotic; fishing/farming; cross-border with Ethiopia (Gambella)

ethnic_groups.name: Fertit (collective)
ethnic_groups.notes: Northwestern South Sudan; Western Bahr el Ghazal; diverse groups including Kreish, Daj, Bongo, Ndogo

ethnic_groups.name: Other (60+ groups)
ethnic_groups.notes: South Sudan has 60+ ethnic groups; Didinga, Luo, Madi, Acholi, Baka, Moru, Avukaya, and many others

independence.notes: World's newest country; followed 2011 referendum (98.83% voted for independence)

country_profile.notes_unique: World's youngest country (independent 2011); largest swamp in Africa (the Sudd); massive oil reserves supply ~98% of government revenue; endured civil war from 2013 to 2018.

natural_resources.notes: Oil dominates economy (~98% of government revenue, ~60% of GDP); pipeline through Sudan to Port Sudan for export (transit fees contentious); Sudd wetland (Africa's largest swamp); vast unexploited agricultural potential; timber reserves; White Nile hydropower potential.

military.notes: SSPDF (South Sudan People's Defence Forces); merged with opposition fighters (SPLA-IO) under 2018 peace agreement; ethnic Dinka/Nuer divisions within military; UNMISS peacekeeping force (~19,000); arms embargo (partially lifted); political-military elite control.

debt_aid.notes: World's youngest nation (2011); humanitarian crisis (famine risk, 7.7 million food insecure); oil production declined from 350k to ~135k bpd; Revitalised ARCSS peace agreement (2018); transitional government (elections delayed); inflation ~300%+.

education.notes: One of the world's lowest education indicators; conflict closed majority of schools; 2.8 million children out of school; extreme teacher shortages (South Sudan had 20x fewer teachers per capita than regional average); English language of instruction but most teachers trained in Arabic.

diaspora_migration.diaspora_population: 2.3 million+ refugees (Uganda, Sudan, Ethiopia, Kenya, DR Congo)
diaspora_migration.notes: Second-largest refugee crisis in Africa; 2.3 million refugees plus 1.8 million IDPs; Bidibidi settlement in Uganda is world's largest refugee settlement; Sudanese refugees fleeing 2023 Sudan war crossing into South Sudan; remittances via informal channels.

digital_economy.notes: Extremely limited telecom infrastructure; Zain and MTN operators; no submarine cable (landlocked); relies on satellite and fibre from Uganda/Kenya; internet extremely expensive; mobile money adoption growing from very low base; power outages limit connectivity.

current_leader.name: Salva Kiir Mayardit
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: SPLM; Dinka (Rek); former SPLA commander; signature black hat from George W. Bush; civil war with Machar 2013–2020

vice_president.name: Riek Machar
vice_president.title: First Vice President
vice_president.notes: SPLM-IO; Nuer; former rival in civil war; Revitalised Agreement on the Resolution of the Conflict (R-ARCSS) 2018

910.name: Early Nilotic Peoples
910.description: Nilotic peoples settle the Sudd and upper Nile region; pastoralist and agro-pastoralist communities including Dinka, Nuer, and Shilluk ancestors.

sub_clusters.name: Nilotic Peoples Migration
sub_clusters.description: Nilotic-speaking peoples migrate from Nile Valley into the Sudd wetlands and surrounding highlands.

sub_clusters.name: Pastoral Society Development
sub_clusters.description: Dinka, Nuer, and other Nilotic groups develop cattle-centred cultures; seasonal transhumance in Sudd region.

920.name: Shilluk Kingdom and Pre-Colonial States
920.description: Shilluk Kingdom as the most centralised pre-colonial state; Azande kingdoms; Dinka and Nuer segmentary societies.

sub_clusters.name: Shilluk Kingdom (Chollo)
sub_clusters.description: Shilluk Kingdom along White Nile founded by Nyikang; divine kingship (reth); most centralised Nilotic state.

sub_clusters.name: Azande Kingdoms
sub_clusters.description: Azande kingdoms in western Equatoria; Avungara ruling clan; resistance to slave raiding.

sub_clusters.name: Dinka and Nuer Segmentary Societies
sub_clusters.description: Decentralised Dinka and Nuer societies; cattle culture; age-set systems; prophetic leadership.

930.name: Slave Trade and External Incursions
930.description: Turco-Egyptian invasion; devastating slave raids (zariba system); European explorers; Mahdist conquest.

sub_clusters.name: Turco-Egyptian Conquest
sub_clusters.description: Muhammad Ali's Egypt conquers Sudan; southern raids for slaves and ivory; zariba trading stations devastate populations.

sub_clusters.name: Ivory and Slave Raiding Era
sub_clusters.description: Khartoum-based traders devastate southern populations; Zubayr Rahma Mansur; massive depopulation and suffering.

sub_clusters.name: Mahdist Conquest of the South
sub_clusters.description: Mahdist state extends control over parts of the south; resistance by Azande and other groups; Emin Pasha relief expedition.

940.name: Anglo-Egyptian Condominium
940.description: British reconquest; Southern Policy separates north and south; minimal development; missionaries and education; Juba Conference 1947.

sub_clusters.name: Condominium Rule in the South
sub_clusters.description: Anglo-Egyptian Condominium; British 'Southern Policy' isolates south from Arab north; Christian missionaries; English language introduced.

sub_clusters.name: British Southern Policy
sub_clusters.description: Closed Districts Ordinance separates south; intention to attach south to British East Africa; policy reversed at Juba Conference 1947.

sub_clusters.name: Juba Conference 1947
sub_clusters.description: Southern leaders pressured into union with north for Sudanese independence; seeds of future conflict sown.

950.name: First Sudanese Civil War
950.description: Anyanya rebellion; southern resistance to northern Arabisation and Islamisation; Addis Ababa Agreement grants autonomy.

sub_clusters.name: Torit Mutiny and Anyanya Rebellion
sub_clusters.description: Southern soldiers mutiny at Torit 1955; Anyanya guerrilla movement; brutal northern military campaigns.

sub_clusters.name: Addis Ababa Agreement 1972
sub_clusters.description: Nimeiry and Anyanya sign Addis Ababa Agreement; Southern Sudan Autonomous Region created; fragile peace.

950.name: Second Sudanese Civil War
950.description: SPLA/M under John Garang fights Khartoum; 2 million dead; oil factor; CPA 2005 ends war.

sub_clusters.name: SPLA/M Founded under Garang
sub_clusters.description: John Garang de Mabior founds SPLA/SPLM; fights for united secular Sudan; Nimeiry abrogates Addis Ababa Agreement.

sub_clusters.name: Devastating Civil War
sub_clusters.description: Over 2 million dead; 4 million displaced; famine; Nuer-Dinka split 1991; child soldiers; oil fuels war.

sub_clusters.name: Comprehensive Peace Agreement
sub_clusters.description: CPA signed January 2005; provides for autonomous government and independence referendum; Garang dies July 2005.

960.name: Independence and Modern South Sudan
960.description: Interim period; independence referendum 2011; world's newest country; civil war 2013-2020; humanitarian crisis; fragile peace.

sub_clusters.name: Independence of South Sudan
sub_clusters.description: Independence referendum 9 January 2011; 98.83% vote for separation; independence 9 July 2011; Salva Kiir president.

sub_clusters.name: South Sudan Civil War 2013-2020
sub_clusters.description: President Kiir dismisses VP Machar; civil war erupts December 2013; ethnic violence; 400,000 dead; mass displacement.

sub_clusters.name: Humanitarian Crisis
sub_clusters.description: Worst food crisis in the world; famine declared 2017; millions displaced; child soldier recruitment; sexual violence.

sub_clusters.name: Revitalised Peace Agreement
sub_clusters.description: R-ARCSS peace agreement 2018; Machar returns as VP; transitional government; elections postponed; fragile stability.

sub_clusters.name: Oil Economy and Abyei Dispute
sub_clusters.description: South Sudan depends on oil revenue (98% of budget); Abyei border dispute with Sudan; oil shutdown 2012; economic collapse.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
